title: PiArc L2 scenario
description: One L2 scenario (architecture section 12.3): workspace fixture, mock provider scripts, the actions that drive Core, approval answers and the expected events, files and requests. Field reference and matching rules: docs/engineering/testing.md section 12.

id.description: Equals the file name without extension.

description.description: The behavior the scenario proves, in one sentence that matches its assertions.

capabilities.description: Capability ids of tests/capabilities.yaml this scenario covers.

platforms.description: Platforms the scenario runs on; both when absent.

platform_reason.description: Why a platform is left out; required when platforms excludes one.

files.description: Initial files: relative path (forward slashes) to UTF-8 content.

run_files.description: Initial UTF-8 files relative to the scenario's isolated temporary root.

git.description: Initialize the workspace as a Git repository.

fixtures.description: Files copied byte for byte from the scenarios' fixtures/ directory: relative path in the workspace to the fixture's name (relative, forward slashes). For CRLF, byte order marks, legacy encodings, images and PDFs.

trusted.description: Record a trust decision for the workspace before it opens; untrusted when absent.

git_commit.description: With git: commit the initial files with a fixed identity (T35).

git_branches.description: With git_commit: branches created at the initial commit (T35).

task_limits.description: Smaller Monitor limits for this scenario (T32); Core's defaults otherwise.

web.description: A local web server for WebFetch (T29). {{web}} in page bodies, redirect targets and tool call arguments becomes http://127.0.0.1:<port>, {{web_alt}} the same server as http://localhost:<port>; Core's WebFetch allowlist admits both for these scenarios only.

oauth.description: A mock authorization server and the test OAuth provider piarc-test-oauth on every Agent Host (T29), signing in with this flow.

packages.description: Extension packages installed through Core before the workspace opens (T40): a directory of run_files used in place, made a git repository and cloned (`git`), or packed and installed with the bundled npm (`npm`). Turned on and every executable item confirmed unless `enable` or `confirm` is false.

path.description: The package directory, relative to the run's temporary root (write it with run_files).

mcp_http.description: Streamable HTTP MCP fixture servers by name (T36): `{{mcp_http:<name>}}` in workspace files and run_files is the server's URL; with oauth the server wants bearer tokens from its own authorization server (`mcp_sign_in`).

cloud_providers.description: Configure a cloud API key through the real settings path; model requests remain on loopback mocks.

providers.description: Mock provider endpoints by name; each is its own Pi provider with one model.

sessions.description: Sessions by label; a single session `main` on the only provider when absent.

actions.description: What the runner does, in order.

approvals.description: Answers to Core's approval requests, in order.

relativePath.description: Relative, forward slashes; the loader also rejects `..` segments and drive letters.

configure_as.description: Configure this mock through the Core settings API.

reasoning.description: The imported mock model supports thinking levels.

vision.description: The endpoint's model takes images as input; text only when absent.

context_window.description: The model's context window in tokens (T27); 200000 when absent.

max_tokens.description: The model's largest output in tokens (T27); 4096 when absent.

model.description: The endpoint's model id (T31), sent as `model` in its requests; mock-model when absent.

web_search.description: A server-side web search before the text (Anthropic Messages only, T38).

deferred.description: Create the session on its first input.

cwd.description: Working directory relative to the workspace; the workspace when absent.

settings_model.description: Create the session without a model: the settings' default model and effort apply (T31); provider still names the endpoint the scenario expects.

worktree.description: Create the session in a worktree of its own (T35): optional name and base branch or commit.

instructions.description: What the summary should focus on (`/compact <focus>`, T27).

restart_core.description: Shut Core down, start it again on the same data directory and reopen the workspace; sessions stay closed until resumed.

fork.description: Forks a session at the entry of one of its agent messages (at_text, T26) or before one of its labeled turns (before_turn, T28's branch from here); the new session takes a deferred session label.

sign_in.description: Signs in to the test OAuth provider (T29): the runner follows the authorization page's redirect like a browser, or cancels at the first step; checks the final core/login state, its message and whether the provider is signed in afterwards.

sign_out.description: Signs out of the test OAuth provider (T29).

mcp_sign_in.description: Signs in to an mcp_http server through Core's mcp_login; the runner follows the authorization page's redirect like the user's browser (T36).

advance_clock.description: Moves the task manager's clock forward by this many seconds (T32): foreground timeouts move commands to the background, Monitor timeouts and wakes happen, without real waiting.

stop_task.description: Stops the newest running background task of the session (optionally of one kind) as the panel's stop button does (T32).

open_terminal.description: Opens a terminal for the user in the session as the terminal panel does (T34): a background task of kind terminal, not shared with the agent.

type_terminal.description: Types text into the session's last opened terminal (\r presses Enter) (T34).

share_terminal.description: Shares the session's last opened terminal with the agent, or stops sharing it, as the panel's switch does (T34, ADR-0050).

check_cost.description: Checks a field subset of the session's token usage and cost from Core (T41, R5): the same answer as the usage card (sessionUsage).

check_usage.description: Checks the session's context usage from Core (T27): its categories add up to tokens (always), a field subset, and categories that must be above zero.

check_harness.description: Checks a field subset of the plan and task list of the session's branch (session/history harness), or their absence when fields is null (T26).

rewind.description: Rewinds a session to before one of its labeled turns (T28): checks the preview (every file by its workspace-relative label), answers each conflict (choices), then checks the report; cancel stops after the preview.

undo_rewind.description: Undoes the session's latest rewind (T28) and checks each file's outcome.

check_changes.description: Checks a field subset of the session's Changes view (T28): files in the order the session first wrote them, line counts, degradation.

discard.description: Discards a file's change, or one hunk of it, in the Changes panel (T28); stale sends an outdated version, which must be refused.

switch_branch.description: Continues the session on the branch whose first user message starts with to (T28).

check_branch.description: Checks the user and agent message texts of the session's current branch in order, and a field subset of its branch points (null: none) (T28).

check_files.description: Checks workspace files in the middle of the actions (T28): content, or null for absent.

sweep_worktrees.description: Runs one worktree cleanup now and checks which sessions' worktrees it removed and which wait for the user (T35).

check_worktree.description: Checks a session's stored worktree: a field subset of path (workspace-relative), branch, exists, removed, cleanupDue, confirm; null for none (T35).

remove_worktree.description: Removes a closed session's worktree; discard throws its changes away; succeeds false expects a refusal (T35).

keep_worktree.description: Keeps a session's worktree for another retention period (T35).

check_git.description: Runs git in the workspace and checks its standard output (T35).

search.description: Searches the sessions' messages through Core: the matching sessions (labels, as a set) and texts some snippet contains (T35).

check_commands.description: List the workspace's slash commands through Core (`listCommands`) until the named ones are present and the others absent, at most 10 s (T40).

set_output_style.description: Set the workspace's output style through Core (`setOutputStyle`, T37); no name removes the choice.

set_web_search_key.description: Save a WebSearch backend's API key through Core (`setWebSearchKey`, T38); no key removes it.

turn.description: Label for the turn the input started.

item.description: Label for the queue item it became.

rejected.description: Core must refuse the input with an error containing this text (a UserPromptSubmit hook, T25).

count.description: Wait until this many matching events arrived.

params.description: Field subset of the event's params.

turn.description: params.turnId is the turn with this label.

mode.description: The mode an approved plan continues in (T26).

comments.description: Inline comments sent with a declined plan, anchored at the first occurrence of quote (T26).

subagent.description: The card must come from a subagent of this type (and description) (T31).

answers.description: One answer per question of a question card (T26).

via.description: The answer comes from a system notification's action (T42).

notification_allow.description: Whether the card must offer Allow in its notification (T42).

decision.description: wait leaves the card unanswered: a question form whose timeout answers it (T26).

tool.description: The canonical tool name the request must be for.

call.description: The tool call id the request must be for; L3 runs answer each request with the approval naming its call (T30).

index.description: Request number of the endpoint, from 0.

tools.description: Exactly these tool names, in any order.

tools_windows.description: Exactly these tool names on Windows, where sessions also get PowerShell; tools applies when absent.

same_tools_as.description: Compare the tool definitions byte for byte with an earlier request on the same endpoint (T26).

body.description: Field subset of the request body.

events.description: Ordered subsequence per session; each item a field subset.

files.description: Workspace files after the run: exact content, or null for absent.

configured_providers.description: Assert public fields and chat model availability for each configured provider.

request_counts.description: Exact number of requests each endpoint received.

tool_batches.description: Tool call ids in the batches their Core requests arrive in.

fixtures.description: Workspace files after the run whose bytes equal a fixture file: relative path to the fixture's name.

config_diagnostics.description: Subset of Core's configuration diagnostics of the workspace after the run (T24): `trusted`, and `files` keyed by layer id, each a subset of that file's report (status, effective, overridden, ignored, issues; lists compare element by element).

core_io.description: Core answered a request with this method for this tool call.

absent_on_disk.description: Strings no file under the run's temporary root may contain after the run (T38: a key that must stay in the vault).

json_lines.description: Workspace files of JSON lines after the run (hook fixtures record their stdin, T25): exactly this many lines, each a field subset.
